Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can scope the technical deep-dive: 

- Summary from our side: Redwood can support three serving modes (Hosted API, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, Private VPC / on-prem). Each has tradeoffs across latency, cost, and regulatory controls.
- To recommend the best short- and medium-term path we need a couple details: 
  1) Are you currently using a 3rd-party LLM API for production? If so, which provider(s) and any particular features you rely on (tool calling, streaming, embeddings)?
  2) You mentioned an internal GPU cluster in the demo — can you confirm whether model artifacts live there (e.g., self-hosted checkpoints) or you only use it for custom inference code calling a hosted model?
  3) Compliance/crypto needs: do you require KMS/HSM, dedicated tenancy, or strict data residency?
  4) Expected steady-state and peak QPS (or r/s) and typical tokens per request — helps narrow Dedicated sizing vs. Private sizing.

Hi Irene,

Great demo — thanks. Quick answers inline: 
1) We currently use AltAI's public API for a portion of prod traffic (mainly for embeddings + chat fallback). We also have an internal PyTorch cluster (K8s + custom load balancer) that runs a few internal models and some feature extraction jobs. Model artifacts for certain internal models are stored on-prem on our Ceph cluster.

2) The cluster runs both internal models and wrappers that call AltAI for specific features — so it's a hybrid setup.

3) Compliance: we handle regulated customer PII. We require customer-specific encryption keys (KMS) and VPC isolation for production workloads. On-prem option is preferable for the most sensitive pipelines, but if Redwood can provide VPC + HSM-backed KMS we could consider cloud-first.

4) Traffic: steady-state ~15 requests/sec (avg payload ~1.2k tokens). Peaks up to ~55-65 r/s for short bursts. Latency SLO: tail < 500ms for generation-only paths if possible.

We can do Wed 2026-05-19 at 10:30 PT for the technical deep-dive — will include our infra lead (Tom).

Irene / team / Emma —

Thanks for the context. Below are recommendations based on the constraints and numbers provided. High-level takeaway: start with a short Hosted POC to validate correctness and latency, then move to Dedicated or Private depending on compliance and on-prem requirements.

1) Immediate POC (0-4 weeks): Hosted API
   - Why: fastest to validate parity (tokenization, behavior) against AltAI outputs, no infra setup time.
   - Caveats: Hosted will not meet strict on-prem requirements; for PII-sensitive flows use a dedicated customer tenant and restrict data retention. We can bind a customer-managed KMS (HSM integration) for some use-cases but full on-prem control is limited.

2) Short-to-mid term (4-12 weeks): Dedicated reserved capacity
   - Why: predictable throughput and tail latency control for steady 15 r/s and peak bursts to 65 r/s. We can size a Dedicated pool: estimate ~2 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (continuous) with autoscaling headroom for bursts.
   - Benefits: per-tenant isolation (no noisy neighbor), easier rollout and rollback, and most of your latency SLOs are achievable with tuned batching (we can keep tail ~400-450ms on generation-only paths).

3) Long-term / strict compliance (12+ weeks): Private VPC / on-prem
   - Why: if on-prem is required for certain pipelines (per Emma), Redwood Private offers a customer-controlled control plane and can be deployed in their VPC or on their hardware. This is the most work (networking, VPN, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logging) but satisfies the highest compliance bar.

Migration notes from AltAI API + self-hosted cluster:
- Model artifacts: plan a conversion step — check tokenizers and model configs for parity. For quantized models we'll run a validation suite (our evals harness) against your golden prompts.
- KV cache + session warmup: when cutting over stateful conversational flows consider a staged ramp to avoid cold-cache latency. We recommend 24–72 hour parallel run for session rehydration.
- Data plane: for Private mode we will need to map egress rules and S3/Ceph access. For Dedicated we provide VPC peering and private subnets.

Operational items / ask list for sizing and procurement: 
- Confirm model family and whether you want Redwood to host pre-built open models or deploy your private checkpoints.
- Confirm retention windows and whether any flows require zero-retention.
- Provide a brief list of golden prompts and evals we can run during the POC.

Cost / timeline note (very rough): Hosted POC: low cost (meters per-token) and 1–2 weeks to validate. Dedicated: initial reserved commitment + monthly cost; estimated lead time 3–6 weeks for reserved pool setup. Private: project lead time 6–12+ weeks (networking & compliance integrations).
